findings.conclusion: The complete original argument preparation and Bazel invocation region is byte-equal. PIPESTATUS[0] is captured before new evidence work, and the wrapper explicitly exits with that original value. Selection/collection is in guarded negative conditionals that emit warnings rather than substituting collector status.

Only exact ten allowlisted console target summaries are eligible. PASSED and FLAKY select existing records; SKIPPED, NOT_REPORTED and conflicting summaries do not traverse their old target directories. Failed-target collection remains separate. Cached markers and absent markers are recorded without claiming fresh execution.

The original bounded-scope path validation, nested-link refusal, regular-file requirement, streaming full-byte hash/copy, changing-file checks and exclusive destination creation are retained. The added mtime field records local metadata and does not establish invocation identity.

All thirteen existing test function bodies are byte-equal after ignoring only trailing separators; three new tests exercise actual temporary files, status 0 and 37, missing logs, large binary records, skipped/unreported stale directories and ambiguous reports.

limits: No Python, Bash, Git fixture or Bazel execution was performed in this review; the original sole-lane syntax and complete unittest gates remain required.

A console PASSED summary plus a local file is not independent proof that the file belongs to the current invocation. The manifest explicitly preserves that limit; this collection alone cannot close a case or platform gate.

complete_for_selected_targets reports successful copying of selected existing records, not complete suite or attempt coverage. Cached FLAKY/attempt evidence must retain retries and origin distinctions.
If no allowlisted target is reported, no selected archive is produced. Missing archives remain missing evidence, not implicit success.
No workflow, test budget, filter, cache policy, retry, source permission boundary or Rust production source is changed.
